Kimberly —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and legal at Elanthera want to lock down sequencing across MSA/DPA and the pilot order form so we don’t hit signature blockers at the last minute. High level items we care about:

- Clear acceptance criteria for the pilot (SLA, latency buckets, data retention).
- Which document must be signed first (MSA or Order Form) and whether legal needs to finish DPA review before provisioning.
- Target timelines: procurement would like a 3-week close if exposures are limited.

Can you share a recommended mutual action plan (milestones, owners, and cutover gates)? Also please attach any sample Gantt or milestone spreadsheet you use for similar pilots.

If helpful, we can do a short sync on Thursday.

Thanks,

D.,

Appreciate the clear ask. Attached is a first-pass MAP and a simple Gantt that lays out recommended sequencing and owners. Quick summary of our proposal:

1) Legal review window (MSA) — 7 business days for redlines, then a 3-business-day alignment window. Owner: Redwood Legal (Karthik) + Elanthera legal.
2) DPA parallel review — can run in parallel with MSA review if Elanthera legal confirms no special data residency clauses; otherwise DPA signed prior to provisioning. Owner: legal teams.
3) Order Form (pilot) — signature targeted immediately after MSA agreed; procurement signs order form and we begin provisioning within 48 hours.
4) Acceptance gate — pilot acceptance criteria checklist (latency SLA, sample PII handling, integration test pass) to be completed within the 14-day pilot window.

I’ve included estimated calendar dates in the attached Gantt based on a 3-week close (start = Sep 9). Please review and tell me where you want to compress or expand.

Proposed next step: 30-minute sync Thursday 9/9 at 10am PT to confirm owners and finalize dates. I’ve copied Karthik for legal input.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

D., Kimberly —

Quick legal take to set expectations before the sync:

- MSA review: Redwood can turn on comment-redline feedback within 5 business days for the first pass; Elanthera typically takes 7 business days to return redlines (we will confirm during call). Plan for a total of ~10 business days to reach negotiated text if there are moderate changes.
- DPA: if Elanthera requires additional data-processor addenda (e.g., specific subprocessors or EU SCC additions), that can add 5–7 business days. If it’s standard, we can complete in parallel with MSA and not block provisioning.
- Order Form: we recommend that the MSA (high-level terms) is agreed before final signature on order form to avoid rework on commercial terms. However, we are comfortable executing the order form contingent on MSA redline closure (DocuSign clause to allow signature subject to final MSA confirmation).

I’ll bring a draft MSA redline plan and a short checklist of legal gating items to the call.

—Karthik

Thanks — that level of detail helps. A couple of clarifications:

- Procurement preference is to have the MSA finalized before executing the order form. We are open to the contingent-signature approach Karthik suggested only if we can get a firm timeline and holdback language.
- For DPA, we have one extra requirement: we need a written confirmation from Redwood on subprocessor list and whether any processing will happen outside US-based AWS regions for the pilot. If processing will happen outside US, Elanthera will escalate to security (possible extra review).

We will accept the proposed Thursday 9/9 at 10am PT. I’ll bring procurement + legal (Alyssa + external counsel).
